slides.title: Mode A — The Missed Evening Runs Whole

items.text: If the quarter lost an evening — the snow, the assembly, the bug — tonight runs that session's plan, unchanged
“Tonight is not a make-up class squeezed in. Tonight IS [session name] — whole, unhurried, the evening you were always going to get.”
“Nothing was skipped this year; it just moved.”
The lifted plan runs whole — its blocks, its scripts, its splits; only its closing yields to tonight's quarter-close constants

panel.label: PROVERBS 16:9 (ESV)
lines: “The heart of man plans his way, but the LORD establishes his steps.”

slides.title: Mode B — The Live Rhythm-Card Walk

items.text: If the quarter ran clean, the whole room walks its actual Rhythm Cards aloud — “the real ones, not the ideal ones”
The leaders walk first — and walk genuinely slipped cards honestly; the whole evening stands on that
Two or three minutes each: daily, weekly, monthly, as lived — holds and slips in the same voice
Glad out loud about holds; never guilt about slips — “a slip you noticed is the practice working”
“If you want help with a slip, ask for it, and we will spend a minute on it together. If you do not, name it and keep walking.”
Everyone walks their own card — parents never their teen's; pass-anytime holds tonight like every night
“Listen like a thief. If you hear an idea you want — a time of day, a trick, a place to keep the card — take it.”
“That is not cheating. That is what a fellowship is for.”
One sentence around the circle: one idea you heard tonight that you are stealing — name it, and the person you stole it from
Fast, light — pass-anytime

slides.title: Quarterly Pulse — Back in the Bin

items.text: The return bin sits by the door — drop your Pulse 3 page as you arrive
Nobody watches the bin; nobody is asked whether they dropped a page
Spares sit beside it for those who forgot — a page next week is as welcome as a page tonight
The team reads every page — the Quarter 4 planning conversation starts from what these pages say
The break starts tomorrow — and we have done this before: at Christmas, every one of us carried one practice across the gap, and at The Return we heard what held
Look at your card and choose ONE practice — just one — to carry through this break deliberately
Not the whole card; the whole card can rest — that is sabbath, not failure
Write it in your journal right now — the practice, and when, and where
Then, one sentence around the circle: the practice you are carrying — “speaking it is part of carrying it”
The Returning Rule travels: begin again on the next available day. At The Return II the first question will be the kind one: what held?
